title: Customer status digest & action plan: intermittent partial responses (EU region)
body:
Draft customer-facing status digest and post-incident action plan (concise).

Summary (one line): Intermittent timeouts and truncated streaming for a subset of text-generation requests in the EU region between 2029-10-01 19:12 UTC and 2029-10-02 03:40 UTC, causing partial responses for some customers. Core user-facing behavior was brief stalls or early stream termination; regenerated requests usually returned complete output.

Impacted customers and endpoints:
- Affected: hosted inference streaming and chat endpoints for EU region (region: europe-west-1).
- Symptoms observed: streaming sessions that ended with an abrupt close, truncated final tokens, or a 504-style client observable timeout.
- Scope: ~0.8% of production requests routed through a single routing cluster during the window. Larger payloads (longer contexts) were more likely to surface the issue.

Immediate mitigations we applied (what we did while incident was active):
1) Enabled a temporary routing bypass: traffic that matched the affected selector was redirected to a warmed, higher-capacity pool to avoid the problematic cluster.
2) Rolled back an automated routing change that had been deployed the previous morning and suspected to be the trigger.
3) Activated automatic model substitution for streaming: requests were routed to a lower-latency model variant if the primary stream did not establish within 1.2s. This preserved continuity for interactive flows.
4) Cleared stale prefix/KV cache state on the affected hosts and performed controlled cache-warm operations.
5) Increased short-term capacity for the EU dedicated pool and extended streaming connection timeouts by 30s to reduce client-visible truncations.

Root cause (what went wrong):
- Summary: A recently introduced routing selector optimization (PR referenced above) contained an edge case where certain tenant attributes matched an unintended host group. That host group was running an older kernel path that had a latent memory growth issue under continuous streaming workloads. Under normal load the hosts tripped resource pressure and intermittent stream terminations occurred.
- Contributing factors: lack of a canary gate for routing-selector changes that affect stateful streaming flows; insufficient automated detection for long-tail memory growth in that specific kernel path; cache-invalidation assumptions that did not hold when traffic was abruptly rebalanced.

Customer impact characterization: 
- User-visible: Partial responses and truncated streaming for a minority of requests; those requests could typically be recovered by retrying a generation call. No data loss or model output corruption was detected — only premature session termination.
- Business: No SLO breach for the calendar quarter is expected after adjustments; we are issuing this communication to be transparent and provide guidance for customers that may have observed elevated retry rates.

What we will do next (near-term and long-term fixes):
Near-term (next 72 hours):
- Deploy a fix to the routing selector to prevent unintended host-group matches (hotfix merged and staged; rollout scheduled).
- Add a short-lived synthetic monitor targeting long streaming sessions to detect memory growth within 30 minutes.
- Provide an opt-in flag for customers who prefer conservative routing that avoids warm-up host groups.

Long-term (30–90 days):
- Introduce a canary pipeline for routing policy changes that explicitly exercises long-lived streaming sessions before full rollout.
- Expand runtime telemetry for kernel execution paths and add automated alerts for long-tail memory growth patterns.
- Tighten cache-consistency checks and add a safe drain flow when rebalancing traffic that ensures KV/prefix caches are rehydrated before serving production streams.
- Update our SLA and capacity planning playbook to include an explicit buffer for regions with heavy streaming usage.

Actionable guidance for customers (recommended client-side mitigations):
- Implement idempotent request tokens for generation calls to allow safe retries without duplicate-side effects. We expose X-Request-Id or a similar header; our SDKs already set this by default.
- Use exponential backoff with jitter for retries on streaming interruptions, starting at 200–400ms.
- For critical low-latency paths, consider pinning to a dedicated capacity product (Redwood Dedicated) or use our lower-latency model variants during peak windows. Contact your account rep to discuss capacity reservations.

Customer-facing timeline (high-level):
- 2029-10-01 09:10 UTC: routing selector optimization merged to staging.
- 2029-10-01 18:58 UTC: change promoted to EU canary ring.
- 2029-10-01 19:12 UTC: first customer reports of truncated streams; automated alerts triggered.
- 2029-10-01 19:40 UTC: rotation of traffic began away from affected hosts; mitigations applied.
- 2029-10-02 03:40 UTC: incident considered mitigated; monitoring continued for reoccurrence.

How we will keep you informed:
- Short-term: We will post a consolidated status page update (STATUS-6789) and send a one-time notice to affected tenant contacts.
- Follow-up: A deeper postmortem (internal) will be available and we will publish a customer-facing summary with progress against the long-term items within 30 days.

If you saw an impact
- Recommended first step: retry the request; if you continue to see truncated streams, open a support ticket referencing INCIDENT JIRA-INC-3821 and include one sample request id (X-Request-Id) and timestamps.
- If the affected flow is business-critical, escalate to your assigned account manager or email cs@redwoodinference.com with subject line "URGENT: Streaming truncations — EU".

Contact and support
- Customer Success lead: Aisha Patel (owner of this communication draft).
- Support: cs@redwoodinference.com.
- Incident references: STATUS-6789, JIRA-INC-3821, PR#452.

Notes for internal reviewers (do not include for customers until approved):
- Confirm that the rollout schedule for the routing selector fix prevents an immediate full-region promotion before canary results are collected.
- Coordinate wording with legal if customers request credits.
- Decide whether to offer a one-time assistance review for customers that recorded >5% error amplification during the window.

End of draft.

Document history: Draft prepared by Aisha Patel on 2029-10-02; updated 2029-10-05 with additional telemetry notes and PR link.
